1 أَرِجَ , aor.
اَرَجَ , inf. n. أَرَجٌ (S, A, Msb, K) and أَرِيجٌ (S, A, K) and أَرِيجَةٌ, (K, [in which it is only mentioned as syn. with the first and second of these ns., so that it may be a simple subst.,]) It (perfume) diffused, or exhaled, its odour; (S, A;) as also ↓ تآرّج : (A:) it had a hot, or strong, odour; syn. تَوَهَّجَ رِيحُهُ. (S, A, K.) ―
-b2- It (a place) was, or became, strongly fragrant. (Msb.) ＝
-A2- أَرَجَ: see 2, in three places.
From An Arabic-English Lexicon (Edward William Lane)
